heroHeadline: 'DISINTEGRATING' — RASMUSSEN; TRUMP CONFIRMS POLAND TROOP TRANSFER 'POSSIBLE'; ITALY AND SPAIN DRAWDOWNS IN ALLIED PLANNING; HELSINGBORG FMM MAY 21–22
heroSubtitle: On May 9, 2026, former NATO Secretary General Anders Fogh Rasmussen declared the alliance is 'disintegrating' — the most authoritative former-official condemnation of the breakdown to date — and proposed a new 'coalition of the willing' of nations meeting 5% GDP defense spending with no single-member veto. The same day, Trump confirmed that shifting 5,000 withdrawn Germany troops to Poland is 'possible,' formally validating the coalition shuffle logic. A Bloomberg analysis reported that top NATO diplomats forecast imminent drawdowns from Italy (~13,000 US personnel) and Spain (~3,500 at Rota), plus potential cancellation of US participation in European military exercises. By May 10, allied governments had begun formal contingency planning for post-US infrastructure scenarios. Background: May 8 NPR — 'Something fundamental has broken' (Daalder); May 7 White House CT strategy labeled allies 'terror incubators'; Germany 5,000-troop withdrawal ongoing; NDAA §1249 prohibits reducing forces below 76,000 without congressional authorization. Week of May 7–10: rhetorical rupture advanced to institutional decomposition — former senior officials diagnosing disintegration, US president confirming loyalty-based European footprint, allied capitals operationally planning for NATO without the US. Next: Helsingborg NATO Foreign Ministers Meeting May 21–22, 2026 (first NATO ministerial on Swedish soil); Ankara Leaders' Summit July 7–8.
